title: Improving Counterfactual Generation for Fair Hate Speech Detection
measurement_description: The paper measures fairness and bias in hate speech detection models, specifically evaluating how models perform on sentences containing social group tokens (SGTs). This includes identifying and mitigating bias against religious groups by analyzing stereotypical language and creating semantically plausible counterfactuals to train fairer models.
findings: The study found that by using a pre-trained language model (GPT-2) to evaluate the likelihood of counterfactual sentences, it's possible to generate more semantically sound counterfactuals for fairness training. This method improves fairness metrics for hate speech classifiers, reducing misclassification of non-hateful sentences mentioning religious groups (like 'Jews' or 'Muslims') while preserving the model's ability to detect genuinely stereotypical hate speech targeting these groups.
